title: Local active-parameter presentations of residual full root towers
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, $k$ a characteristic-$p$ field, $Y$ a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], and $B=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ an affine etale chart [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in A$ cut out precisely the distinct reduced irreducible branches of a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$ be affine pro-etale [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ put $B_J=\operatorname{Spec}(A/(t_j)_{j\in J})$ and $R_J=R/(t_j)_{j\in J}$. Set
$$T_J=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R_J[x_{d,n}]_{d\notin J}/(x_{d,n}^n-\bar t_d)_{d\notin J}\right),$$
using the full parameter-root algebra [def-sfb-full-parameter-root-tower], with positive indices ordered by divisibility and power transitions.
Then $B$ and $B_J$ are regular, separated and finite type over $k$. $B_J$ has an affine open cover $W=\operatorname{Spec}A_W$ with a subset $L\subseteq J^c$ for each $W$, such that $\bar t_d$ is a unit on $W$ for $d\notin J\cup L$, and the subschemes $V(\bar t_d)$, $d\in L$, are precisely the distinct reduced integral branches of a strict normal crossings boundary on $W$. The vanishing parameters at every point of $W$ occupy distinct positions in a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters].
Write $R_W=R_J\otimes_{A/(t_j)}A_W$ and
$$D_W=\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R_W[y_{d,n}]_{d\notin J\cup L}/(y_{d,n}^n-\bar t_d)_{d\notin J\cup L}.$$
The map $\operatorname{Spec}D_W\to W$ is affine pro-etale, and there is a canonical isomorphism
$$T_J\times_{B_J}W\ \cong\ \operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}D_W[z_{d,n}]_{d\in L}/(z_{d,n}^n-\bar t_d)_{d\in L}\right).$$
It fixes coefficients, sends each inactive root to the corresponding $y_{d,n}$ and each active root to $z_{d,n}$, and respects every divisibility transition. For every $A_o\subseteq J^c$, it identifies the open inverting $\prod_{d\in A_o}\bar t_d$ with the open inverting $\prod_{d\in A_o\cap L}\bar t_d$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. These identifications commute with ring base change. They hold also after replacing $U$ by $U[P]$ for any profinite $P$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. Empty faces, charts and parameter sets are allowed; no connectedness of $B_J$ is required.

proof.text: First check the finiteness assertions for the base. Since $B$ is affine and $Y$ is separated, hence quasi-separated, the qcqs permanence lemma makes $B\to Y$ quasi-compact. The etale finite-presentation lemma therefore gives that $B$ is finite type over $k$. Both $B$ and $B_J$ are affine, hence separated over $k$. If $A$ is generated over $k$ by $a_1,\ldots,a_m$, their quotient classes generate $A/(t_j:j\in J)$, proving finite type for $B_J$ directly. The boundary definition, including its empty-intersection clause, gives regularity of $B$ and of the scheme-theoretic intersection $B_J$. No connectedness of this intersection is used.

source.place: Tags 03GI and 01KN; etale finite-type consequence; Tag 0BIA in etale.tex for regular intersections

proof.text: We need the named equations, not just unnamed parameters. Fix $x\in B$, put $H=\mathcal O_{B,x}$ and $S_x=\{d:t_d(x)=0\}$. The ideals $(t_d)$ in $H$, $d\in S_x$, are distinct primes: the branches are reduced integral closed subschemes, and distinct branches through $x$ remain distinct after localization. The boundary definition gives regular singleton quotients of codimension one and a regular quotient by their sum of codimension $|S_x|$. Part (a) of the transverse-prime parameter lemma supplies a parameter system $f_1,\ldots,f_h$ with $(f_i)=(t_{d_i})$. Since $H$ is a domain (the regular-normal lemma) and both generators are nonzero, $t_{d_i}=u_i f_i$ for a unit $u_i$: write $t_{d_i}=a_i f_i$, $f_i=b_i t_{d_i}$ and cancel to obtain $a_i b_i=1$. Scaling the first parameters by these units preserves their generated maximal ideal. Thus the actual vanishing $t_d$ occupy distinct positions in a parameter system.

source.place: Tag 0BIA, converse proof, simultaneous branch equations; parameter lemma part (a)

proof.text: Let $x\in B_J$ correspond to a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ containing every $t_j$, $j\in J$. By quotient-localization its local ring is $A_{\mathfrak p}/(t_j:j\in J)$. In the system of step 2 permute the parameters indexed by $J$ to the beginning. The parameter-quotient theorem says this quotient is regular local of dimension $\dim A_{\mathfrak p}-|J|$. The images of the remaining parameters generate its maximal ideal and their number equals its dimension, so they form a parameter system by definition. Every original parameter not vanishing at $x$ is already a unit in $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and stays a unit in the quotient. In particular the images of the remaining vanishing labels occupy distinct positions in a residual parameter system at every point.

Put $A'=A/(t_j:j\in J)$ and $F=\prod_{d\notin J}\bar t_d$. The ring $A'$ is Noetherian since $B_J$ is regular affine, by the affine-open Noetherian lemma. At each point, step 3 writes $F$ as a unit times a product of distinct residual parameters; absorb that unit into one factor when there is a factor, and use the unit ideal when there is none. The boundary-parameter criterion applied to $V(F)\subset B_J$ shows that this is a reduced strict normal crossings boundary. Its labels may be disconnected or reducible. The labelled-root geometry lemma explicitly permits such labels and applies by step 3: for each $x\in B_J$ it supplies an affine neighbourhood $W$ and $L=\{d\notin J:\bar t_d(x)=0\}$ with all inactive labels units, and with the active labelled zero schemes precisely distinct reduced integral branches on $W$. These neighbourhoods cover $B_J$.

source.place: Tag 0BIA; labelled finite-root geometry, local active/inactive neighbourhood clause

proof.text: Fix such a $W$ and set $K=J^c\setminus L$. The ring $R_W$ represents the base change $U\times_B W$: the affine fibre-product formula identifies it with $R\otimes_A A_W$, since $A\to A_W$ kills $(t_j:j\in J)$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}R_W\to W$ is weakly etale by base change from $U\to B$. For each positive prime-to-$p$ integer $n$, put $E_n=R_W[y_{d,n}:d\in K]/(y_{d,n}^n-\bar t_d)$. Every $\bar t_d$, $d\in K$, is a unit, and $n$ is a unit because Bezout gives integers $a,b$ with $an+bp=1$ and $p=0$ in $R_W$. Adjoin the finitely many $y_{d,n}$ successively. The unit-binomial lemma makes each adjunction finite etale, hence ind-etale. Ind-etale stability makes $R_W\to E_n$ ind-etale and then $R_W\to D_W=\varinjlim_nE_n$ ind-etale, hence weakly etale. Compose with $\operatorname{Spec}R_W\to W$. Since both spectra are affine the resulting morphism is affine. This proves the required affine pro-etale assertion in the weakly etale convention of the stated site.

source.place: Tags 097J, 097K, 097L and 097N; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PL, unit-root algebra

proof.text: The root-tower base-change lemma and the affine fibre-product formula identify $T_J\times_{B_J}W$ with the spectrum of $H=\varinjlim_n R_W[x_{d,n}:d\in J^c]/(x_{d,n}^n-\bar t_d)$. Let $G=\varinjlim_nD_W[z_{d,n}:d\in L]/(z_{d,n}^n-\bar t_d)$. Construct a homomorphism $H\to G$ by fixing $R_W$, sending $x_{d,n}$ to $y_{d,n}\in D_W$ for $d\in K$ and to $z_{d,n}$ for $d\in L$. Each equation is satisfied; for $n\mid m$ the images satisfy $y_{d,m}^{m/n}=y_{d,n}$ and $z_{d,m}^{m/n}=z_{d,n}$. Polynomial evaluation, descent through the defining quotient, and the colimit universal property therefore give the homomorphism.

source.place: Polynomial evaluation and quotient universal properties; compatible-root presentations; agent generator construction

proof.text: Conversely the compatible substitutions $y_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,n}$ induce $D_W\to H$. At each active-root stage use this coefficient map and $z_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,n}$ to obtain a map to $H$; these maps respect every transition, so induce $G\to H$. Both composites fix coefficients and every named root. Polynomial evaluation uniqueness, quotient surjectivity, and colimit uniqueness make the composites identity. The resulting ring isomorphism gives the claimed scheme isomorphism by contravariance of $\operatorname{Spec}$. This argument also explains why the single divisibility index on each tower suffices: any finitely many root indices admit their least common multiple, still prime to $p$, as a common index.

source.place: Universal properties applied in both directions to the compatible-root generators; agent argument

proof.text: For $A_o\subseteq J^c$ write $\prod_{d\in A_o}\bar t_d=u\prod_{d\in A_o\cap L}\bar t_d$, where $u=\prod_{d\in A_o\cap K}\bar t_d$ is a unit of $R_W$ and of both tower algebras. Inverting $u f$ is the same as inverting $f$: the forward map uses $f^{-1}=u(uf)^{-1}$ and the reverse uses $(uf)^{-1}=u^{-1}f^{-1}$. These maps fix coefficients and are inverse by the fraction definition of localization. The ring isomorphism of steps 6-7 fixes every $\bar t_d$, so gives exactly this identification of principal opens, with the scheme-theoretic open structures as well as the underlying sets.

For any ring base change, the root-tower base-change lemma identifies the base-changed full tower, inactive tower, active tower, and indicated principal opens with the presentations having the new coefficients. On both routes around each comparison square a coefficient goes to its image in the new ring and a named root goes to the correspondingly named root. The uniqueness properties used in steps 6-7 make the square commute; the same computation is unchanged for each power transition. Finally the profinite clause of that lemma gives $U[P]=\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}LC(P,\mathbf Z))$ affine pro-etale over $U$, and identifies its root algebras and opens with this very base change. Repeat step 5 for this new affine pro-etale chart and use the commuting squares just checked. If $B_J$ is empty, take the empty cover; for $L=\varnothing$ or $K=\varnothing$ the corresponding root algebra is its coefficient ring. All generator and localization formulas still apply for the zero ring, empty profinite parameter, empty $J$ and empty boundary.
